name: File System Access: open and save pickers
plain: Lets the person pick files and then read and write them in place; Chromium only.
meaning: A site can open a local document, edit it and save over the original, like a desktop app. The person picks the file, and the browser asks again before write access.

access.prompt_ui: Chrome file chooser, then Edit files / Save changes permission bubble
access.persistence: Handles can be stored in IndexedDB; Chrome 122 offers Allow on every visit persistent permission
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Not available in cross-origin iframes (SecurityError); secure context
steps: Chrome shows file chooser (and a Save changes prompt for write)
Page reads or writes through the handle

limits.headline: Can open files you pick and save changes back to them, in Chrome and Edge
limits.user_action: You click Open file or Save as, pick, and later click Allow.
can: Save changes in place, once you allow saving
Create a new file where you choose in Save as
Remember a file to reopen it later, but ask you again for permission
cannot: See other files in the same folder
Change the file before you allow saving
Pick sensitive locations such as system folders
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge on computers only. Firefox, Safari and phones do not have it.

story.what_it_is: Lets you pick files, then the site reads and writes them in place (Chromium only).

marketing.name: File System Access API
marketing.pitch: Google pitches it as a way for web apps to open and save files on your computer like desktop apps.

marketing.name: Browser FS Access
marketing.pitch: Chrome shares a helper that gives web apps native style open and save windows when the browser allows.

story.for_you: A system window opens so you choose a file. Pick it, and the site can save changes back to the same file. The browser asks again after you close the tab.
story.for_makers: It makes web apps feel like desktop apps, with open, save and save as. That helps web editors and tools replace installed software. It only works in Chromium browsers today.

use_cases.example: A web photo editor opens your image, lets you edit, and saves back to the same file.
A web drawing tool lets you open and save sketches on your disk.
A browser game editor opens a map file and saves it back as you work.
A web text or code editor opens a file and saves changes in place.
A music tool opens a project file and writes the changes without making a copy.
A scam page asks to save a file to a sensitive place. Browsers refuse many locations.
A company web app edits spreadsheets in place on a shared drive.

technical_bounds: Needs transient user activation and a secure context
Chrome and Edge 86 only (no Firefox, no Safari); Safari and Firefox expose only OPFS
Write access prompts after the pick (Edit files? bubble); permission lasts until all tabs of the site close, or persistent in Chrome 122
Chrome blocks picking system files and some folders (for example files in system directories and executables like .exe and .bat are warned or blocked for writing)
startIn can name well known folders (desktop, documents, downloads, music, pictures, videos) or reuse an id; the page cannot read the full path

abuse: Ransomware style bulk writes (mitigated by prompts and blocklist)
Planting a malicious file after a deceptive save prompt

history.change: Persistent permissions for handles (Allow on every visit)
Dangerous file types blocked for write in some cases
